rv.q: The piece survives on the imperishable Berlin songs and the charm of the performers.
The main drawback, though, is that stuffing the piece with so many extra songs stretches the whole thing to two and a half hours
I suspect they'll wonder what all the fuss was about.
This production may play it too safe, but in moments like these, it is easy to see why Top Hat was such a hit when it first graced stages back in 2011 and continues to charm.
Instead, a perfectly enjoyable tourist class version evokes the movie instead of breathing the magic.
Tap your troubles away in a wondrous world of spectacle, exotic locations, sumptuous costumes, breathtaking dancing and unforgettable numbers. A scintillating box of treats!
With its toe-tapping talent and old Hollywood charm, Top Hat is a dazzling delight.

cn.t: Critics find this stage adaptation a charming but safe crowd-pleaser elevated by Irving Berlin's songs and impressive tap dancing, though some feel it's overstuffed and old-fashioned, lacking the sparkle of the original film.
